topic.title: Learning on Manifolds and Geometric Function Spaces
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: Some data and representations live naturally on curved spaces rather than ordinary Euclidean vectors. This topic develops neural layers, optimization, density models, and operators that respect that geometry. Residual connections, transport, wavelets, and manifold-valued regression provide different ways to preserve meaningful notions of distance and direction.
topic.whyItMatters: Comparing features in incompatible local coordinates can lose information or create artificial differences. Geometry-aware methods aim to make transformations and optimization correspond to the structure of the objects being modeled.
topic.evolution: Early representatives investigate manifold density estimation and latent-space distance preservation. Later work develops hyperbolic representations, Riemannian residual networks, and flows on manifolds. Recent studies extract geometry from scores and build vector-diffusion wavelets, extending geometric modeling from point locations to directional fields and structured operators.
openQuestions: When does explicit geometric structure improve transfer enough to justify its computational cost?
How can learned manifolds be validated when the true geometry is unknown?
